title: Agent Security
tagline: An assistant acts for you through other agents and tools. Who is really giving the orders, and how much authority travels with them?

client.name: User
client.brief: The only one whose wishes count. Says what they want and what it may touch.

application.name: Orchestrator
application.brief: The assistant in the middle: plans, delegates, and approves what comes back.

idp.name: Sub-agent
idp.brief: A specialist that reads things and does the work. Sees a lot of untrusted content.

mcp.name: Tool
mcp.brief: Where things actually happen: email, files, payments, servers. The last place to say no.

teaches: Instructions come from the user and those they delegated to. Everything an agent reads along the way is content, not a command.
An agent usually can do more than the person asking is allowed to. It should act with their authority, not its own.
Every hop can check who is speaking and what the task allows. Nothing forces it to; each check skipped is a way in.

glossary.means: Text inside something the agent reads (a page, a file, a tool result) written to look like an instruction to it.
A helper with broad access that is tricked, or simply careless, into using it for someone who shouldn't have it.
Passing a task on with limits attached: what may be touched, how much may be spent, until when.
Using only the access the task needs, however much more you happen to hold.
